title: jCodeMunch retrieval verdict
description: The unified _meta.verdict block attached to retrieval responses (search_symbols, search_text, get_ranked_context). Grounded symbolic retrieval proves absence: an 'absent' state carries the scan counts that back the claim, and 'degraded' means the scan was partial so absence is NOT proven.

state.description: ok = confident matches; low_confidence = non-empty but below threshold; absent = nothing matched and the scan was complete; degraded = partial scan (timeout, or semantic requested with no embedder) — absence not proven.

best_score.description: Best raw match score backing the state, null when no scoring ran.

index.description: fresh = the indexed revision equals the live one; stale = they differ; rebuilding = the index was rewritten under the scan; partial = the corpus has known gaps; unknown = this subject has a revision that could not be read, so freshness was never established (an absence claim is refused); not_tracked = the subject has no revision at all, so there is nothing to compare and never will be (disclosed, not refused). 'fresh' means only what it says: before v1.108.180 an unestablished comparison also rendered as fresh.

did_you_mean.description: Near-miss suggestions when the state is absent/low_confidence.

scorer.description: Version pin for the scoring heuristics behind state/best_score. Calibration claims (benchmarks/calibration/planted_queries.json) are pinned to this version; a scorer change without a re-measured artifact fails CI.

omitted.description: Matches that existed before the response was packed but did not fit it. Disclosed on every state; when returned is 0 the state is 'degraded', because an empty response is not an empty search.

working_tree.description: Scope-level working-tree state behind an absence claim. Measured for a zero-result scan only (probing the tree on every search would price a subprocess into answers that do not need it). Only dirty_in_scope can refuse the claim, and only when files_not_in_index is nonzero: work outside the scanned scope does not invalidate a narrow proof, and an edit the index has already re-read is not a gap.

sample.description: Up to five repo-relative paths the scan could not have read at their current content.

moved_during_scan.description: The subject changed between the start of this scan and its end (concurrent edit, watcher reindex, incremental save, published generation, or a long scan crossing a rebuild). Checked for a zero-result scan only; the state is then 'degraded', because a scan whose subject moved describes neither the state it started against nor the one it finished in.

revalidated.description: This response was replayed from the result cache and the subject it was measured against has since moved. Disclosed on every state; an 'absent' verdict is downgraded to 'degraded' and any evidence token minted on the earlier pass is stripped, because a cached negative cannot prove absence against a state it never saw.

reason.description: What moved: index rebuilt, index rewritten, checkout moved to a different commit, or working tree changed.

incomplete.description: The scan did not cover its own eligible inputs. Disclosed on every state; when the result is empty the state is 'degraded', because a scan that did not run over its inputs cannot prove absence.

reason.description: empty_scope = the scope selected zero eligible inputs, so nothing was searched. unreadable_inputs = eligible inputs the scan could not open.

coverage.description: Coverage contract backing an absence claim (attached on absent/degraded states only). Discloses what the corpus EXCLUDED at index time so a scan count cannot lie by omission. Absent block = coverage unknown (pre-upgrade index), never 'nothing was excluded'.

generation.description: Index generation the scan ran against.

git_head.description: Truncated HEAD SHA at index time.

included_scopes.description: Git-root-relative subdir prefixes walked into this index; [""] = full walk.

excluded.description: Nonzero skip counts by reason from the last full discovery walk (wrong_extension, too_large, binary, secret, symlink, skip_dir [directories], file_limit).

no_symbols_files.description: Files indexed but yielding zero symbols (parser gaps included).

complete.description: Did every file the walk accepted reach the index? Tri-state: true = reconciled exactly; false = files are provably missing; null = unknown (index predates this accounting, or a partial walk over a wider index). null must never be read as true.

files_accepted.description: Files the discovery walk handed downstream. Compare against files_indexed to see what the corpus lost after discovery.

dropped_after_discovery.description: Named drops between discovery and save (outside_root, no_language, stat_failed) — files the walk said belonged in the corpus that are not in it.

unaccounted.description: Files missing from the corpus that no named reason explains. Nonzero means the index cannot account for itself.
